question: Which of the following elements is NOT present as a diatomic molecule in nature?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Helium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Hydrogen is regarded as diatomic because it has two hydrogen atoms in its molecule, but **helium is considered monoatomic **since** it has one atom in its molecule**.
 
• Due to its totally filled valency shell structure, **helium has no chemical affinity.** **Helium cannot form a diatomic molecule.**
 
• Since **helium belongs to noble gases, it has an electron-filled outer shell.**
 
• **Helium (He) is an inert gas **and a chemical element belonging to **Periodic Table Group 18 (noble gases)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Monatomic gas**

 
 
• **​Monatomic is a compound** word made up of the letters "mono" and "atomic," which **stand for a single atom**. This phrase refers to the gases as monatomic gases and is used in both physics and chemistry. 
 
• **Due to their lack of reactivity, noble gases are considered monatomic gases.**
 
• **Examples of monatomic gases: **Helium (He), Radon (Rn), Neon (Ne), Xenon (Xe), Argon (Ar) and Krypton (Kr).
 
 
 
• **Diatomic molecules**
 
 
• **​Diatomic molecules are ones that have just two atoms in them**. A diatomic molecule is referred to as homonuclear if it is made of only one element, and as heteronuclear if it is made of two separate elements.
 
• **Examples of Diatomic molecules: **Hydrogen (H₂), Nitrogen (N₂), Fluorine (F₂), Oxygen (O₂), Iodine (I₂), Chlorine (Cl₂) and Bromine (Br₂).
